title: Matrix multiplication and fast powers
summary: Multiply matrices with three nested loops, then compute M^n in O(log n) multiplications.
hints: `C = A * B` where `A` is `n x k` and `B` is `k x m` gives an `n x m` matrix: `C[i][j] = sum over t of A[i][t] * B[t][j]`. That is three nested loops: `i`, `j`, and the inner sum over `t`. Allocate `C` first - `n` rows, each `make([]int64, m)` - which starts zero-filled.

Exponentiation by squaring: start with `result := Identity(n)` and `base := m`. While `exp > 0`: if `exp` is odd (`exp&1 == 1`), `result = Multiply(result, base)`; then `base = Multiply(base, base)` and `exp >>= 1`. That is O(log exp) multiplications instead of exp of them.

For Fibonacci use `Q = Mat{{1, 1}, {1, 0}}`. `Q^n = {{F(n+1), F(n)}, {F(n), F(n-1)}}`, so `Fibonacci(n)` is the entry `[0][1]` of `MatPow(Q, n)`. Doing it in `int64` is exact up to `F(92)`; beyond that Go quietly wraps around (no panic, no warning), which is exactly why the tests stop at 90.
